about: The priest says “meum ac vestrum sacrifícium” — my sacrifice and yours — and in one phrase divides what he immediately calls one thing: sacrifícium stands in the singular. The answer hands the sacrifice back to him: “de mánibus tuis”, from thy hands. It is the longest answer the servers give the priest — only their own Confíteor is longer, and that is a prayer of theirs rather than an answer — and the only one in which they set out what the sacrifice is for: the glory of God's name, our own good, the good of the whole Church. The rubric has the priest say the invitation “with his voice raised a little”, and the closing Amen in a low voice; when no one answers, he answers himself.

s01.narrative: The priest kisses the altar and turns to the people; he spreads and joins his hands, and, as the rubric directs, raises his voice a little.

s02.translation: Pray, brethren, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God, the almighty Father.

s03.narrative: The server answers, or those present; if no one answers, the priest says the response himself, saying meis — my — for tuis.

s04.translation: May the Lord accept the sacrifice at your hands for the praise and glory of His name, for our good also and the good of all His holy Church.

s05.narrative: The priest answers in a low voice — the last word of the offertory he says to himself alone.

w001.function: A plural imperative: the priest speaks to everyone present.

w002.function: Vocative; in the plural it sounds the same as the nominative and the accusative.

w004.function: Neuter, because it agrees with “sacrifícium” (w007), not with any masculine noun.

w007.function: Singular in spite of the two modifiers: mine and yours, but one sacrifice.

w008.function: Predicate after “fiat” (w009): that it may become acceptable.

w014.function: The same verb with which the priest began both “Súscipe” prayers — here a subjunctive of wish, of the Lord in the third person.

w019.function: The answer hands the sacrifice back to the priest: he called it “mine and yours”, they say “from thy hands”.

w025.function: The reflexive possessive: his own, that is, the Lord's who receives. It agrees with “nóminis” (w024).

w030.function: One written word carrying two: totíus with the enclitic -que (“and”). The enclitic draws the stress onto the syllable before it.

w033.function: Three ends named in order: God's glory, our own good, the good of the whole Church.
